source.description: Project parser/load point where the attacker-controlled CoolKey object class attribute is read from the card object into obj_class.

sink.description: Out-of-bounds stack READ when memcpy copies pubkey-sized data from a prkey_info stack object.

root_cause.description: The EC private-key branch sets obj_type to SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC while obj_info still points to prkey_info, creating a type/size mismatch.

fine_trace.note: ASan reports a stack-buffer-overflow READ when memcpy reads pubkey_info-sized bytes from the smaller prkey_info stack object.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The attacker controls CoolKey object attributes returned through the fuzzed card reader. In the private-key branch, sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init sets obj_info to the stack variable prkey_info. For EC keys, the vulnerable code incorrectly sets obj_type to SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PUBKEY_EC. sc_pkcs15emu_object_add later uses obj_type to choose sizeof(sc_pkcs15_pubkey_info) as data_len, but the data pointer still references sc_pkcs15_prkey_info. memcpy therefore reads beyond the prkey_info stack object, producing the observed stack-buffer-overflow.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch changes the EC private-key branch to use SC_PKCS15_TYPE_PRKEY_EC, keeping obj_type consistent with obj_info = &prkey_info. The object-add helper then selects sizeof(sc_pkcs15_prkey_info), so memcpy copies only the actual source object size.
